messages:
noah: Small heads-up: while auditing the migration guide I saw both 'API key' and 'token' used. That's going to confuse enterprise customers. Can we standardize on 'API key' for auth and add a glossary note about tokens being broader?

ingrid: Agreed. Also propose adding a short 'naming exceptions' section to STYLEGUIDE for infra terms that must keep historical names (e.g., 'dedicated' capacity).

sasha: For docs snippets, let's avoid renaming any config keys that are consumed by infra. Only local variable and comment changes.

luis: I can add a quick grep rule to the PR to verify no config keys were changed. Will add to CI checklist.

style-bot: style check: found 8 instances of 'token' used for API keys; suggested replacements: 6/8 automated, 2 manual review needed.

noah: I'll open a PR that replaces the 6 obvious ones and list the 2 manual ones for discussion. Will include a short blurb in the migration guide (non-breaking) explaining the user-facing terminology choice.

ingrid: Thanks. Also add 'auth' glossary alias pointing to 'API key'. And a note: when in doubt use the more specific term (API key) in tutorials.

sasha: Add me as reviewer for any snippet that touches auth examples.

luis: Adding a pre-merge grep to detect changes to config files under /deploy. That should prevent accidental infra changes.

noah: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/900 (wip). Tagging @sasha @luis for the infra checks.
